ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the line $y=-2x+a$ intersects the $y$ axis at point $A$ and intersects the line $y=x+1$ at point $P(3,b)$. Point $B$ lies on the line $y=x+1$. Find a point $C$ on the $x$ axis such that the value of $AC-PC$ is maximized. Please write the coordinates of point $C$ and find the maximum value.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} When points $A$, $P$, and $C$ are collinear, the maximum value of $AC-PC$ is equal to $AP$. Solving $0 = -2x + 10$ gives $x = 5$, thus $C(5,0)$.\\
Since $P(3,4)$,\\
$AP= \sqrt{AH^{2}+PH^{2}}=\sqrt{(10-4)^{2}+3^{2}}=\boxed{3\sqrt{5}}$.
